answer: The protocol stops farms with a synchronized liveness round. At a random instant it opens a short pulse: every identity must finish an interactive puzzle a single human can complete only once before the window closes. The interval is too tight to hop between keyboards, so one operator cannot march an ocean of sockpuppets through the same beat. Each extra vote needs another attentive person for the whole session, plus a one-time saffron credential bound to a live face check that cannot be cloned. The attacker's cost is wages and burned credentials, not cheap new wallets.
